title: Superposition and the Hadamard Gate
summary: The states |+⟩ and |−⟩, measurement and a quantum random number generator.
objectives: Turn a qubit into an equal superposition and measure it
Judge from a list of counts whether a generator is fair or biased
Say why |+⟩ and |−⟩ look the same in a measurement and how a second Hadamard gate separates them
mission: Build a 3-bit quantum random number generator. Put all three qubits in an equal superposition and measure each qubit into the classical bit with the same index. The 8 outcomes (000 to 111) must be equally likely.
hints: What does a qubit need to give 0 and 1 equally often? Equal-sized amplitudes, which is a point on the equator of the Bloch sphere. Which gate takes you there from |0⟩?
The Hadamard gate does it, one call per qubit. Then every qubit has to be measured into a classical bit: qc.measure(qubit, bit).
qc.h(0), qc.h(1), qc.h(2), then qc.measure(0, 0), qc.measure(1, 1), qc.measure(2, 2). A loop over range(3) saves typing.

prediction.question: You measure |+⟩ 10,000 times instead of 100. How does the number of zeros compare with the 100-shot case?
options: It stays within about 5 of half the shots, as before
It is about 50 away from 5,000: more counts off, but a smaller fraction off
It lands on 5,000 exactly, because so many shots remove the fluctuation
prediction.explanation: The standard deviation of the count is √(N p (1−p)) = √(10000 / 4) = 50, ten times larger than the 5 of the 100-shot case. Relative to N it falls from 5% to 0.5%. The count never becomes exactly N/2 in a reliable way: the fraction converges, the count does not.

challenge.mission: Build biased bits. Measure each qubit into the classical bit with the same index so that bit 0 is 1 with probability 1/4, bit 1 is 0 or 1 with probability 1/2, and bit 2 is always 1, all three independent. Only ry, h, z and id are allowed, and ry, h and z must appear. The distribution of the 8 outcomes must match this product distribution within a total variation distance of 0.05.
hints: A qubit in cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + sin(θ/2)|1⟩ gives 1 with probability sin²(θ/2), and ry(θ) prepares it from |0⟩. Which θ makes that 1/4?
sin²(θ/2) = 1/4 gives θ = π/3. Qubit 1 keeps its Hadamard gate. Qubit 2 needs a certain 1 and X is not allowed, but H, then Z, then H does the job: Z takes |+⟩ to |−⟩ and H takes |−⟩ to |1⟩.
qc.ry(pi / 3, 0), qc.h(1) and qc.h(2), qc.z(2), qc.h(2). Then measure each qubit into the classical bit with the same index. Import pi from math.
